A seed that snores underground by day and wakes with its thorns raised once the sun is gone. Witches have planted these in place of fences for ages. Tuck a handful of black wool over it and, whatever it dreams of, it grows frightfully overnight.
흰 양 떼 사이에서 혼자 검은 양. 달이 없는 밤에도 털이 희미하게 빛나: One black sheep in a flock of white. Its wool glows faintly even on moonless nights, and it seems rather proud of that. The wool is an offering for old rites, and the thorn barricades' favorite snack.
검은 양에게서 깎아 낸 털입니다. 손에 쥐면 달빛처럼 서늘하고, 가시 씨: Wool shorn from the black sheep. It feels cool as moonlight in the hand, and the ground stirs a little when you lay it over a thorn seed. Do not stuff a pillow with it. The dreams get far too vivid.
산장 목장에서 깎은 평범한 양털입니다. 평범하다는 게 이 산에서는 귀한: Ordinary wool from the lodge pasture. Ordinary is a rare virtue on this mountain. Village traders claim a witch's wool keeps you warmer, and the witch has never bothered to correct them.
숲이 내어 준 나무입니다. 벽에 난 구멍을 막고, 무너진 제단을 받치고,: Wood the forest gave up. It patches holes in the walls, props up fallen altars and feeds the hearth on cold nights. The witch will not deny that the lodge still stands thanks to timber more than magic.
등에 가지가 돋고 이끼가 자라는 숲의 괴물입니다. 쓰러뜨리면 그 그림자가: A forest monster with branches on its back and moss in its fur. Fell it, and its shadow obeys the witch for a while. Come morning light it forgets everything and turns back into a tree. It may once have been a guardian of the woods.
북쪽 마녀가 눈 위에 손가락으로 그리는 달의 문양입니다. 서리는 소리 없: A moon sigil the witch of the north draws on the snow with one finger. The frost spreads without a sound and seizes the ankles of anyone who steps on it. Ask why winter sides with the witch, and she will not answer.
굽은 장대 끝에 매단 마녀의 등불입니다. 기름 대신 오래된 약속으로 타오: A witch's lantern hung from a crooked pole. It burns on old promises instead of oil, pushing back the fog and making the things in the dark hesitate. Any guest walking at night likely found the lodge by this light.
산장의 문장으로 봉한 초대장입니다. 받은 이는 자기도 모르게 짐을 꾸리고: An invitation sealed with the lodge's crest. Whoever receives it finds themselves packing a bag and climbing the mountain. Who will arrive, nobody knows until the door opens. The witch says that is the only fun part of running an inn.
아직 털도 제대로 안 난 새끼양입니다. 목장에 들이면 이틀 내내 울타리에: A lamb that has barely grown its wool. Put it in the pasture and it will spend two days headbutting the fence, then one morning it is simply grown. That is how sheep are.
산장에서 하룻밤 묵고 도끼를 빌려 간 손님과의 약속입니다. 나무를 베는: A promise from a guest who spent a night at the lodge and borrowed an axe. They hum while felling trees and hold the timber close until the witch comes by. When night falls, they are the first to knock on the door.
활을 메고 산장에 묵은 손님과의 약속입니다. 낮에는 눈 위의 발자국을 쫓: A promise from a guest who arrived with a bow. By day they follow tracks in the snow, by night they nock arrows from the shadow of the roof. Apologies to the rabbits, but the stew is delicious.
검 한 자루로 밥값을 하겠다는 손님과의 약속입니다. 낮에는 산장 둘레를: A promise from a guest who means to earn their supper with a sword. By day they circle the lodge trampling snow; when something moves in the dark, they charge without asking. The witch sometimes worries a little, watching them go.
숲을 제집처럼 아는 손님과의 약속입니다. 아침에 바구니를 들고 나가 저녁: A promise from a guest who knows the forest like their own kitchen. They head out with a basket at dawn and return before dusk, not entirely sure themselves what is inside it. On a lucky day there is a chest.
사냥꾼과 채집가가 들고 온 고기입니다. 상인에게 넘기면 동전이 되고, 모: Meat brought back by the hunter and the gatherer. Hand it to a trader and it becomes coin, set it over the campfire and it becomes stew, and in a pinch the witch just eats it. Her stomach is sturdier than it looks.
Stew simmered over the front-yard campfire. Potato, salt, mushroom, and meat. Meat costs extra, though the witch never charges a wounded mercenary. One bowl puts back most of the blood lost in a night.
눈처럼 하얀 토끼 가죽입니다. 마을 아낙들이 겨울 목도리감으로 제일 좋아: A rabbit pelt white as snow. Village folk prize it for winter scarves. The rabbit was not consulted.
채집가가 눈 속에서 파낸 낡은 상자입니다. 자물쇠는 오래전에 녹슬어 떨어: An old chest the gatherer dug out of the snow. The lock rusted off long ago, and three things someone once hid lie sleeping inside. Choose one and the others vanish to wherever lost things go. Chests are like that.
아직 먼지를 털지 않은 유물입니다. 뒤집어 보기 전까지는 보물인지 잡동사: A relic still under its dust. Until it is turned over, no one knows whether it is treasure or junk.
달이 가장 밝은 밤에 은실로 묶어 둔 부적입니다. 지니고 있으면 마녀의: A charm bound with silver thread on the brightest night of the moon. Carry it, and the light that leaves the witch's fingertips reaches farther and bites harder. Why the moon helps witches, only the moon knows.
어느 오래된 산장의 화로에서 꺼져 본 적이 없는 돌입니다. 손에 쥐면 겨: A stone that has never gone cold in the hearth of some ancient lodge. It stays warm in the hand even in winter, and set nearby, it lets the lodge's wounds close slowly through the night. Homes are kept like this, the stone seems to say.
숲에서 가장 오래된 나무가 쓰러지며 남긴 심장입니다. 이걸 지닌 벌목꾼의: The heart left behind when the oldest tree in the forest fell. An axe swung by whoever carries it sinks in as if the trees were stepping aside. We choose to believe the forest allows it.
늑대 송곳니를 가죽끈에 꿴 목걸이입니다. 걸고 있으면 사냥꾼의 눈이 밝아: A wolf's fang on a leather cord. Wearing it sharpens a hunter's eyes and roughens a swordsman's hands. Wolf-kin frown at the sight of it, so tuck it under your collar in front of guests.
서리 여왕이 단 한 번 흘렸다는 눈물입니다. 아니, 전설이 그렇다는 겁니: The single tear the Frost Queen is said to have shed. Or so the legend goes. Keep it close and the air around the lodge slows, and every morning a fresh frost sigil blooms on the windowsill.
붉은 갓에 흰 점이 박힌, 누가 봐도 먹으면 안 될 버섯입니다. 마녀는: A red cap with white spots, a mushroom anyone can tell you not to eat. The witch eats it. Her stomach turns, but a forgotten card floats up from the bottom of her pouch. Wisdom or stubbornness, you decide.
가죽 표지가 다 닳은 마법서입니다. 누가 쓴 건지는 첫 장이 뜯겨 알 수: A spellbook with its leather cover worn through. The first page is torn out, so the author is anyone's guess. Open it and the cards in the witch's pouch rise above the pages, each clamoring to be picked. Time holds its breath meanwhile.
숲의 이끼를 감아 만든 붕대입니다. 상처에 대면 흙냄새가 나면서 아물고,: A bandage wound with forest moss. Press it to a wound and it heals with a smell of earth, drawing out the foul things that seeped into your pouch as well. A trick from the witch of the east, and it works just fine in the north.
송진을 듬뿍 먹인 횃불입니다. 던지면 눈 위에서도 한동안 꺼지지 않고 타: A torch soaked in pine resin. Throw it and it keeps burning a good while, even on snow. The things in the dark hate fire. Once, so did the witches.
유리병에 모아 둔 반딧불이 떼입니다. 마개를 열면 안개 속으로 퍼져 나가: A swarm of fireflies kept in a glass jar. Pull the cork and they spread into the fog, outlining whatever was hiding there. By morning they each go their own way, so leave the jar empty.
숲 바닥에서 잠자던 덩굴을 깨우는 주문입니다. 덩굴은 잠을 깨운 걸 꽤: A spell that wakes the vines sleeping under the forest floor. The vines resent being woken, and take it out on the nearest ankle. Best hope it belongs to an enemy.
겨울을 나려고 가을 내내 쌓아 둔 단단한 장작입니다. 벽에 구멍이 나면: Hard firewood stacked all autumn for the winter. When a hole opens in the wall, it goes into the hole instead of the stove. That is how the lodge's walls get a little thicker every year.
달빛 돌 제단에서 양털을 바치고 받은 수의입니다. 이 천을 덮은 이는 그: A shroud granted at the moonstone altar in exchange for wool. Whoever is covered by this cloth will not open the door when death comes calling that night. Only once. Death does not knock twice.
제단에 가시를 바치고 얻은 권능입니다. 손을 땅에 대면 눈 아래 잠든 가: A power earned by offering thorns at the altar. Touch the ground and every thorn sleeping beneath the snow wakes at once, seizing all it can reach. When the snow melts in spring, someone always asks what happened to the field.
붉은 만찬의 의식이 남긴 잔입니다. 비어 있는데도 늘 무겁지요. 이 잔을: The chalice left by the rite of the Red Feast. It is empty, yet always heavy. On a night the witch holds it, the wounds she deals flow back to close her own. What price it asks, no one yet knows.
빈 굴의 주인이었던 거대한 짐승의 털가죽입니다. 겨울잠을 자던 것을 고대: The pelt of the great beast that ruled the empty den. Something ancient woke it from hibernation, and the witch put it back to sleep. Drape it over the lodge roof and the fur takes half of everything, night wind and enemy claws alike.
침식된 자가 산장 벽에 손톱으로 새긴 기도문입니다. 읽을 수 없는데도 자: A prayer scratched into the lodge wall by one of the Eroded. It cannot be read, yet you keep reading it; thrown away, it is back in your pouch. Only a moss bandage or a market day's sunlight will wipe it out.
맹독 곤충이 마녀의 옷자락에 남기고 간 포자입니다. 눈에 잘 보이지도 않: Spores a venomous insect left on the hem of the witch's robe. Barely visible, yet every dawn her throat is raw and her fingertips tingle. Not enough to kill, is the witch's diagnosis, but nothing to leave alone either.
보스가 울부짖던 소리가 귓가에 남은 것입니다. 아침이 와도 그 소리가 머: The echo of a boss's howl, lodged in the ear. Even when morning comes the sound fills the head, and reaching into the pouch never crosses the mind. Until it is cleansed, the witch quietly drinks her tea.
늑대 수인 파르그가 검은 양 한 마리 값으로 두고 간 병입니다. 자기 피: A vial the wolf-kin Fargh left in exchange for one black sheep. He said it was his own blood. Drink it and it hurts terribly for a while; afterward you feel the moon wax and wane on your skin. Fargh only said it was 'a fair trade.'
늑대의 피가 마녀 안에 남긴 첫 번째 달입니다. 가늘게 뜬 초승달 아래서: The first moon the wolf's blood left inside the witch. Under a thin crescent her hands move faster than her eyes. The witch herself grumbles that she has no idea why her hands are so busy.
늑대의 피가 남긴 두 번째 달입니다. 반쯤 찬 달 아래서는 다리가 먼저: The second moon the wolf's blood left behind. Under a half moon the legs run first and the head catches up later. A lap around the lodge takes noticeably less time.
늑대의 피가 남긴 마지막 달입니다. 보름달이 뜨면 마녀는 로브를 벗어 던: The last moon the wolf's blood left behind. When the full moon rises the witch throws off her robe and runs the snowfield on four legs. Claws cannot open a pouch, so that night is settled with teeth. Back at dawn, the witch never speaks of it.
국경 수비대가 쓰던 장검입니다. 녹은 슬었어도 날은 아직 서 있고, 손잡: A longsword once carried by the border guard. Rusted, but the edge still holds, and someone's name is half worn off the grip. Put it in a mercenary's hand and their eyes change a little. The witch does not take up swords. That is not her way.
벼락 맞은 참나무 가지를 깎은 지팡이입니다. 벼락은 나무 속에 조금 남아: A staff carved from an oak branch struck by lightning. Some of the lightning stayed in the wood, so when the witch casts with it, the light stings a bit more at the tip. Good for leaning on, too. The mountain is steep.
양털을 겹겹이 누빈 솜옷입니다. 칼날도 추위도 한 겹씩 느려지지요. 산장: A gambeson quilted with layer upon layer of wool. Blades and cold alike slow down one layer at a time. The lodge's sheep look somehow hurt when they see it, but it is still better worn than not.
먼 길을 걸어온 나그네가 산장에 두고 간 장화입니다. 바닥이 닳아 있는데: Boots a traveler left at the lodge after a long road. The soles are worn through, yet somehow your step is lighter in them. Did the traveler leave barefoot? The witch did not ask.
붉은 마가목 열매를 실에 꿴 부적입니다. 마을 할머니들이 아이 목에 걸어: Red rowan berries threaded on a string. It looks exactly like the ones village grandmothers hang around children's necks. Wear it, and wounds close a little at a time when no one is looking. The grandmothers were right all along.
고블린 그라즈의 사촌과 그 사촌의 친구와 그 친구의 사촌들입니다. 밤에: Graz the goblin's cousin, his cousin's friend, and that friend's cousins. Whistle at night and they pour in from somewhere, bite the nearest enemy, and go home at dawn. Mercifully, they do not stay for breakfast.
고블린 타크의 주머니에서 나온 수상한 통입니다. 안에 뭐가 들었는지 타크: A suspicious canister from Tak the goblin's pocket. Even Tak is not entirely sure what is inside. Throw it and it goes off with a bang that sends enemies fleeing, though now and then an ally loses an eyebrow. Goblin-grade 'mostly safe.'
고블린 폭죽 중에 제대로 안 터진 녀석입니다. 버리기는 아깝고 들고 있기: A goblin firecracker that failed to go off properly. Too good to throw away, too nerve-wracking to keep. Toss it and it pops with a small thud, leaving whoever it hits dazed for a moment. Goblins call this a success too.
고블린 피클이 숫자 세기를 포기하고 생각해 낸 작전입니다. '전부 저기로: The plan Pikl the goblin came up with after giving up on counting. 'Everyone, over there!' That is the whole plan. The more gang members, the better it works; with none, Pikl just stands there looking sheepish.
유리구슬과 동전을 잔뜩 붙인 고블린의 미끼입니다. 어둠 속의 것들은 왜인: A goblin lure studded with glass beads and coins. For some reason the things in the dark cannot resist a sparkle. Neither can goblins. Once everyone has gathered round, the lure bursts in a blinding flash.
고블린 러스크가 고물을 쌓아 만든 방책입니다. 못과 끈과 '대충'으로 지: A barricade Rusk the goblin piled up out of junk. Held together by nails, string and 'close enough.' Enemies pound on it before the lodge, probably because it looks like the easier target. It collapses on its own after two days.
고블린 사냥꾼 피클이 아끼는 덫 세 개입니다. 밟으면 발목을 물고 잠깐: Three traps dear to Pikl the goblin hunter. Step on one and it bites the ankle and will not let go for a moment. With a goblin at the lodge they get reset every dawn, though Pikl admits to catching his own foot twice.
고블린 타크가 주머니를 정리하다 넘겨준 자루입니다. 목재인지 가죽인지 고: A sack Tak the goblin handed over while cleaning out his pockets. Timber, pelts or meat, shaking it tells you nothing. Sometimes there is scrap metal mixed in, which Tak calls 'a bonus.'
녹슨 못, 휜 숟가락, 정체 모를 쇠붙이입니다. 고블린에게는 보물이고 마: Rusty nails, a bent spoon, metal of unknown origin. Treasure to a goblin, junk for the trader to the witch. Neither is wrong.
그라즈 할아버지가 손주에게 물려준 호루라기입니다. 고블린이 불면 사촌들이: A whistle Grandpa Graz passed down to his grandson. Blown by a goblin, the cousins trickle in one by one; blown by anyone else, it is just loud. Family is like that.
냄비를 두드려 펴서 만든 고블린식 투구입니다. 맞을 때마다 찌그러져 점점: A goblin helmet hammered out of a cooking pot. Every blow dents it a little more until it barely blocks anything. A goblin hammers it flat again each morning. Everyone else just thinks it is a waste of a good pot.
골동품 수집가 말라가 쓰던 작은 저울입니다. 동전을 올리면 무게가 아니라: A tiny scale that belonged to Mala the antique collector. Set a coin on it and it weighs not the metal but 'how much more you could get.' A mercenary carrying it always finds one more coin in a fallen enemy's pocket.
Mala's treasured monocle. Through it, everything shows its price: a fallen enemy's pockets, a pebble on the ground, occasionally the person standing next to you. On a mercenary, far less loot goes unnoticed.
요정들이 장난삼아 하는 바꿔치기입니다. 손에 쥔 걸 눈 깜짝할 새 전혀: The swap trick the fae play for fun. Whatever you hold becomes something entirely different in a blink. Usually it is something useful, but on a day the fae are in a mood, it is not. The mood of the fae cannot be known.
요정이 잠결에 들은 숲의 꿈을 받아 적은 기록장입니다. 마녀가 베개 밑에: A journal where a fae wrote down the forest's dreams, half asleep. Sleep with it under your pillow and the morning's draw appears in your dreams ahead of time. The handwriting is dreadful, but it has never been wrong.
엉겅퀴 가시를 엮어 맹세의 표로 삼은 요정의 장신구입니다. 이걸 찬 이가: A fae token of oath woven from thistle thorns. Enemies grazed by the weapon of whoever wears it hesitate, as if their feet caught on thorns. A fae oath is a light thing. The thorns are not.
요정 용병이 어느 저녁 조심스레 꺼낸 부탁입니다. 숲을 조금만 쉬게 해: A request a fae mercenary made carefully one evening: let the forest rest a little. Set the axe down for a day and the forest answers with gifts of its own. The fae do not forget a kept promise, nor a refused one.
자루에 조상의 룬을 새긴 드워프의 망치입니다. 밤새 부서진 벽을 새벽마다: A dwarven hammer with ancestral runes cut into the haft. Each dawn it sets about mending whatever broke in the night. In a dwarf's hands it works twice as hard. Anyone else is better off letting the hammer work alone.
드워프가 산을 넘으며 메고 다니는 흑맥주입니다. 한 잔이면 밤새 맞아도: The black ale dwarves carry over the mountains. One mug makes you sturdy enough to take a beating all night, though anyone not a dwarf finds their legs a little heavy. Dwarves say that is 'the taste of ale.'
드워프 석공이 놓는 성벽의 기초입니다. 기초만으로도 이미 산장 벽보다 단: The foundation of a wall laid by a dwarven mason. Even just the foundation is sturdier than the lodge walls. With several dwarves about, stones broken in the night are quietly replaced each morning. They know how to talk to stone.
대대로 물려 온 드워프의 둥근 방패입니다. 표면의 흠집 하나하나가 조상들: A round dwarven shield handed down through generations. Every scratch on its face is an ancestor's battle. Held by a dwarf, it covers the comrades standing beside them too. That is how the ancestors taught it.
갱도를 받치던 굵은 버팀목입니다. 산장 옆에 세워 두면 지붕이 한결 든든: A thick prop that once held up a mine shaft. Set beside the lodge, it makes the roof feel much safer. It does not go quietly when it breaks, but crushes the enemies around it. Dwarven timber works to the very end.
드워프가 돌에게 불러 주는 낮은 노래입니다. 노래가 이어지는 동안 산장도: A low song dwarves sing to stone. While it lasts, neither lodge nor wall nor barricade will budge. With several dwarves the harmony holds longer. Nobody understands the words.
가죽을 팽팽히 메운 오크의 전쟁 북입니다. 북소리가 울리면 용병들의 팔에: An orcish war drum stretched tight with hide. When it sounds, strength fills the mercenaries' arms, and orcs fight shoving enemies back outright. The sheep sleep badly that night.
솥째 내놓고 다 같이 먹자는 오크의 잔칫상입니다. 차리기만 하면 어디선가: An orcish feast table: bring out the whole pot and everyone eats. Set it and bowls of stew appear from somewhere. More orcs, more bowls. The dishes do not pile up. Orcs do not do dishes.
뼈에 피로 새기는 오크의 맹세입니다. 맹세한 오크는 평생 더 강하게 싸우: An orcish oath carved into bone with blood. An orc who swears it fights stronger for life, but can never afterward be sent away or offered at the altar. That is what an oath means to an orc. The witch knows its weight.
오크 용병이 저녁에 뼈를 던져 밤을 점치는 일입니다. 뼈가 떨어진 모양으: The evening ritual of an orc mercenary casting bones to read the night. The way they fall tells what is coming, or so they say. Whether to prepare, or to know and still gamble on fate, is the witch's call.
적이 쓰러질 때마다 오크의 목에서 터져 나오는 함성입니다. 한 번 외칠: The roar that bursts from an orc's throat each time an enemy falls. Every shout makes the next blow faster, and the one after that faster still. By the end of the night it carries across the mountain.
오크 용병이 조상의 발자국을 따라 하루만 걷고 오고 싶다고 청한 일입니다: An orc mercenary's request to walk the path of their ancestors for a single day. Let them go, and they return at the next dawn with something changed in their eyes. How far they went, they do not say.
오크 주술사가 모닥불 재로 가슴에 그려 주는 문양입니다. 이 문양을 지닌: A sigil an orc shaman draws on the chest with campfire ash. When its bearer falls, the enemies around them flee in a sudden, groundless terror. The shaman explains it as 'the ancestors getting angry.'
꼬챙이에 통째로 꿰어 굽는 오크식 잔치 요리입니다. 고기가 꽤 많이 들어: An orcish feast dish roasted whole on a spit. It takes a fair amount of meat, but the mercenaries get back every drop of blood lost that night and swing harder on a full stomach. The only worry is the smell drifting into the forest.
무리의 냄새가 밴 수인의 털 장신구입니다. 수인끼리 모여 있으면 서로의: A tuft of fur steeped in the scent of the pack. When beast-kin gather, they catch each other's scent and their feet quicken. On anyone else, it is just fur that smells.
짐을 절대 내려놓지 않는 수인 짐꾼의 등짐입니다. 메고 있으면 손이 두: The pack of a beast-kin porter who never sets a load down. Wear it and you gather as if your hands had doubled, and the heavier the load, the faster you walk. Porters call it 'instinct.'
수인 용병이 자꾸 하품을 하다 겨울잠이 쏟아진다고 털어놓은 일입니다. 재: A beast-kin mercenary, yawning again and again, confesses that hibernation is coming on. Let them sleep and they will not wake until the next dawn, but afterward few wounds trouble them. Wake them, and you simply have a tired beast-kin.
인간 용병이 아는 이에게 써 주겠다는 소개장입니다. 이 편지를 들고 산을: A letter of introduction a human mercenary offers to write to someone they know. The next guest climbing the mountain with it will be of the folk the witch hoped for. Decline, and the mercenary looks a little hurt and presses a few coins into your hand 'for the ink.'
도장이 찍힌 직업 길드의 증서입니다. 이걸 내밀면 나무꾼이 사냥꾼이 되고: A guild writ with the seal stamped on. Present it and a woodcutter becomes a hunter, a hunter a swordsman. Same person, new trade, and they act as if they had done it all their lives. Such is the power of a guild seal.
산 아래 마을에서 횃불을 들고 달려온 민병들입니다. 마녀를 돕는 게 무서: Militiamen who ran up from the village below with torches. They are not sure whether they fear the witch or the enemy more, but they copy the fighting style of whoever stands beside them. At dawn they go home and tell tall tales.
인간 용병이 숲에서 주워 온 낡은 기록입니다. 마녀사냥 이전의 글씨체지요: Old records a human mercenary found in the forest, written in a hand from before the witch hunts. Read them and a forgotten folk's wisdom surfaces; close them and the foul things in your pouch settle quietly. Either way, the records do their work.
길 위의 순례자가 산장 문턱에 남기고 간 축복입니다. 마녀를 전설이라 믿: A blessing a pilgrim left on the lodge's threshold. Rather effective, for a prayer from someone who thinks witches are a legend. The foul things in your pouch clear away, and the rumors down the mountain brighten a little.
인간 용병이 아는 상인의 마차가 산장 앞에 멈춰 선 일입니다. 포장 안에: A merchant's wagon, run by someone the human mercenary knows, pulls up in front of the lodge. Under the canvas are goods from distant lands, and the merchant names a price, naturally. Including the trouble of climbing all the way up.
드워프의 흑맥주와 오크의 고기를 한데 싼 전투 식량입니다. 두 종족이 같: A battle ration of dwarven ale and orcish meat wrapped together. It only comes about when both folk lodge under the same roof. Mercenaries who eat it stay sturdy all night and heal a fair bit. Opinions on the taste are divided.
묘지의 제단 아래서 나온 검은 단검입니다. 누군가를 바치면 산장은 조금: A black dagger unearthed beneath the graveyard altar. Offer someone with it and the lodge gathers darker rumors, while cards from beyond the grave enter the witch's pouch. It does not work on an orc sworn by blood. The oath came first.
쓰러지거나 바쳐진 이가 남긴 몸입니다. 카드에는 그 사람의 이름이 적혀: The body left by one who fell or was offered. The card bears their name. Lay it on the ground at night and it rises as a skeleton to fight until dawn. After a day it returns to the earth. Perhaps that is for the best.
무덤 흙을 움켜쥐고 외치는 짧은 명령입니다. 그 밤에 쓰러진 용병들은 눈: A short command shouted with a fistful of grave soil. Mercenaries who fall that night cannot close their eyes and rise again as bare bones. Only at dawn do they finally rest. The witch sleeps poorly on nights she uses it.
뼈를 엮어 세운 음산한 방책입니다. 세우려면 시체가 필요하고, 곁에서 적: A grim barricade of woven bone. Raising it takes corpses, and every enemy that dies nearby lends its bones to make it sturdier. Guests fall silent when they pass it.
희미한 빛이 갇힌 봉인된 병입니다. 시체 하나를 병 속에 거두면 그 혼이: A sealed jar holding a faint light. Gather a corpse into it, and the soul pulls a few cards up from the bottom of your pouch. Shake the jar and something taps softly from inside. Do not shake it.
언데드 아군에게 차려 주는 음산한 만찬입니다. 식탁에 오르는 건 시체이고: A grim feast laid out for undead allies. Corpses are what goes on the table, and the skeletons who partake perk up and swing harder. The witch does not sit at this table. She does not look at it either.
묘지의 무덤이 한꺼번에 열리는 행진입니다. 산장의 소문이 '악명'까지 어: A march in which every grave in the cemetery opens at once. Only possible after the lodge's rumors have darkened to infamy. Every corpse you have kept rises as a skeleton army and walks the night. The villagers shut their windows tight.
뼈만 남은 날랜 사냥개들입니다. 시체 하나를 던져 주면 둘이 일어나 겁먹: Swift hounds of nothing but bone. Toss them a corpse and two rise, chasing the frightened enemies first. Whether they were hounds in life, no one knows. They do not fetch, so do not throw a ball.
산 아래 마을에서 산장을 두고 떠도는 흉흉한 소문입니다. 소문이 음산해지: Ugly rumors about the lodge, drifting around the village below. Once the talk turns grim, a piece of it seeps into the witch's pouch each dawn. Guests have heard it too, and raise their price. Cleanse it, and the talk dies down a little.
바친 이들의 이름을 적어 두는 검은 장부입니다. 마녀가 지니고 있으면 이: A black ledger that records the names of those offered. While the witch carries it, every so often a reply arrives from beyond the grave as the names pile up. The witch does not write the entries. They write themselves.
산장을 거쳐 간 여러 종족의 문장을 한 천에 기운 깃발입니다. 바느질은: A banner stitched from the crests of every folk that has passed through the lodge. The sewing is clumsy, but hang it up and mercenaries of different folk square their shoulders and fight harder. The banner says what kind of place this is.
여러 종족의 말을 받아 적어 온 통역사의 깃펜입니다. 마녀가 지니면 용병: A quill that has taken down the words of many folk. When the witch carries it, mercenaries bring up each other's stories more often than their own folk's. Whether that is the pen's doing or the ale's is unclear.
네 종족 넘게 한 지붕 아래 모인 밤에만 열리는 산장의 축제입니다. 술과: A festival the lodge holds only on a night when four or more folk gather under one roof. Ale, meat and song cost a fair bit of gold, but the mercenaries who share that night are never quite the same after. Nights like this are rare in snowbound mountains.
지나가던 낯선 손님이 문 앞에 두고 간 선물입니다. 포장을 풀면 아직 산: A gift a passing stranger left at the door. Unwrap it and inside is something from a folk that has never yet visited the lodge. Decline, and the stranger leaves a few coins instead. They never did give a name.
용병들이 팔을 걷어붙이고 산장을 한바탕 치우자고 나선 날입니다. 구석에서: The day the mercenaries roll up their sleeves and insist on cleaning the lodge. No telling what will turn up in the corners, so even the witch is a little tense. It is also a chance to pick one thing from your pouch you will never need again, and be rid of it for good.
술 냄새를 풍기며 산장에 굴러 들어온 떠돌이 술꾼 에린입니다. 어디서 났: Erin the wandering drunk, who rolled into the lodge reeking of liquor. She dumps a clatter of bottles from who-knows-where on the table and says 'take what you like.' Even Erin does not know what is in there. There is always at least one rant mixed in.
목으로 넘어가며 불이 붙는 독한 에일입니다. 마신 용병은 그 밤 미친 듯: A strong ale that catches fire on the way down. A mercenary who drinks it fights like mad that night, and the first few blows literally burn. Next morning they clutch their head and cannot move for a while. Erin says that is normal.
벌꿀로 빚은 금빛 꿀술입니다. 손님에게 한 잔 대접하면 그 손님은 기분: Golden mead brewed from honey. Serve a guest a cup and they happily pay extra, then return the next day with something from their homeland. The rarest of Erin's bottles, and the only one without a story attached.
푸른 도깨비불이 병 속을 떠다니는 독주입니다. 손패의 카드 하나에 부으면: A spirit with a blue will-o'-wisp drifting inside the bottle. Pour it on a card in your hand and it either doubles or rolls back into the pouch, one or the other. The wisp never says which in advance. That is why gamblers love it.
새벽 이슬로 담근 맑은 술입니다. 한 모금에 주머니 속 카드 하나를 영원: A clear liquor brewed from dawn dew. One sip and a card in your pouch is forgotten forever. The next morning the head is foggy and the hands a little slow. For anyone with something they want to forget, that is a fair price.
취한 에린이 늘어놓는 횡설수설입니다. 듣다 보면 손에 쥔 게 뭐였는지 헷: Drunken Erin's rambling. Listen long enough and you forget what you were holding, stuff it back in your pouch and pull out something else. It is not a drink, so it does not count toward calling Erin. Erin has three versions of the rant.

A discount would've sat worse with me.
I don't leave debts behind.
죽기 전에 그러더군.\n'불빛을 따라가면 마녀 집이 나온다.\n그러면 살:
Before he died, he told me:
'Follow the light and you'll find a witch's house.
It means you survived.'
마을 약초꾼이 그러던데요,\n마녀가 사는 집 둘레엔\n겨울에도 달맞이풀이:
The village herbalist told me
that evening primrose blooms in winter
around any house where a witch lives.
One more cup of tea tomorrow morning, please.
I'll pay. In herbs.
잡초치고는 너무 예쁜걸요?\n책에선 상처에 좋다던데…\n조금만 캐 가도:
Far too pretty for a weed, isn't it?
The book says it's good for wounds…
May I take a little? I'll leave the roots.
약초꾼 할머니 책이요.\n첫 장에 이름이 찢겨 있었어요.\n…마녀가 쓴:
The old herbalist's book.
The name on the first page was torn out.
…Could a witch have written it?
이 집 수프 말이오.\n국경 역참 셋을 돌았는데\n여기가 제일 낫소. 고:
About the soup here.
I've been through three border waystations
and this is the best. Even without meat.
One more bowl. Paying this time.
…Don't tell the caravan captain.
알고 있소. 벽에 써 있더군.\n…내일 내가 사슴을 잡아 오면\n추가 요:
I know. It's written on the wall.
…If I bring down a deer tomorrow,
the extra charge is waived, yes?
마녀 집 수프인데 겁 안 나?: Not afraid of a witch's soup?
Spent all my fear in the forest.
None left over
to waste on soup.
옛 산길에 돌 이정표가 있소.\n마녀사냥 전에 세운 거지.\n글자 대신:
There's a stone marker on the old road.
Raised before the witch hunts.
No letters, just a lantern sigil.
The room away from the window again.
The sound of a bolt is a fine lullaby.
그 길은 아직 쓸 수 있어?: Can that road still be used?
쓸 수 있소. 나 말곤 아무도 모르지.\n그 문양이 가리키는 끝이\n이:
It can. Nobody but me knows it.
And where the sigil points
is this house.
…아니오. 길잡이는 지우는 게 아니오.\n지운 사람들이 길을 잃었지.\n:
…No. You don't erase a waymark.
The ones who did got lost.
That's how I make my living.
역참에 편지가 쌓여요.\n받는 이가 '숲의 마녀'인데\n보내는 사람은 아:
Letters pile up at the waystation.
Addressed to 'the witch of the forest,'
but nobody admits to sending them.
Didn't lose the road or a letter today!
…Now where did I put my bag.
저, 전 안 읽어요! 배달부니까요!\n…봉투 겉에 '고맙습니다'만\n열:
I, I don't read them! I'm a courier!
…But about ten envelopes
just said 'thank you' on the outside.
진짜요? 그럼 배달료는요?\n…아, 아니에요! 공짜로 할게요.\n이 집은:
Really? Then what about the fee?
…Ah, no! I'll do it for free.
The tea here is too good.
폐허 문양을 베끼다 알았소.\n새긴 손이 둘이오.\n마녀의 손과… 다른:
I noticed it while copying the ruin's sigils.
Two hands carved them.
A witch's hand… and another.
I'll run short of ink again.
The forest keeps adding to the story.
If it's about warlocks, forget you saw it.
…과연. 책은 그들이 사라졌다 하고\n돌은 그들이 있었다 하지.\n나는:
…I see. Books say they vanished,
stones say they were here.
I'm the sort who trusts stones.
그 기록은 어디에 둘 거야?: Where will you keep that record?
책으로는 안 내오. 마녀사냥도\n책 한 권에서 시작됐으니.\n이 집 난로:
Not in a book. The witch hunts
started from a single book, after all.
Beside your hearth should be safe.
장터 소문이에요.\n'마녀네 양털은 비에 안 젖는다'고.\n…사실이에요?:
Market gossip.
'The witch's wool never gets wet in rain.'
…Is it true? It sells for double.
I can pay the lodging in wool, right?
…No? Alright, coin it is.
에이, 그 말은 장터에서 하지 마세요.\n값이 반으로 떨어져요.\n제 몫:
Oh, don't say that at the market.
The price would drop by half.
My cut included.
If it's double, half is mine.
하하, 역시 산장 주인이시네요.\n…좋아요, 셋으로 나눠요.\n양도 한몫:
Haha, spoken like a true innkeeper.
…Fine, three ways.
The sheep deserve a share.
우리 드워프는 마녀사냥 때\n산문을 닫았소. 편도 안 들고.\n…그걸 자:
We dwarves shut the mountain gate
during the witch hunts. Took no side.
…Nobody brags about it.
The house is sturdy.
As long as its owner isn't weaker than the walls.
현명? 돌은 현명하지 않소.\n돌은 그냥 서 있지.\n우린 그때 돌이었소:
Wise? Stone isn't wise.
Stone just stands there.
We were stone back then.
…이 집 문은 내가 지키지.\n늦은 값이오.\n드워프는 빚을 오래 기억하:
…I'll guard this door myself.
Late payment.
Dwarves remember a debt a long time.
장터에서 내기를 했소.\n'마녀는 빗자루로 난다'에\n동전 열 닢. 자,:
I made a bet at the market.
Ten coins on
'witches fly on broomsticks.' Show me.
Next bet will be an easy one.
Who snores first tonight.
The broom is for sweeping the yard.
…젠장! 열 닢 날아갔군.\n내일 내가 마당을 쓸겠소.\n빗자루 값은 해:
…Damn! Ten coins gone.
I'll sweep your yard tomorrow.
Might as well earn the broom's keep.
I'll show you tonight. For a fee.
하! 그 말투, 드워프 같군.\n좋소, 밤에 봅시다.\n못 날면 두 배로:
Ha! You talk like a dwarf.
Fine, tonight then.
If you don't fly, I take double.
이 집 들보 말이오.\n나이테를 세어 봤소. 삼백 년.\n마녀사냥보다 오:
About the beams in this house.
I counted the rings. Three hundred years.
Older than the witch hunts.
Tomorrow I'll fell only straight-grained trees.
You just trust the beams.
그럼 됐소. 좋은 손이었군.\n쐐기 하나 없이 짰어.\n…내 솜씨로도 어:
Then that settles it. Good hands.
Joined without a single wedge.
…Hard even for my skill.
낡았으니 바꿔야 할까?: They're old. Should I replace them?
Replace? These?
…Innkeeper, wood gets harder with age.
Opposite of people.
밤새 안 잤지. 눈 밑이 검어.\n우리 광산에선 그런 얼굴을\n'갱도 유:
You didn't sleep. Dark under the eyes.
Back in our mine we called that face
'the mine-shaft ghost.'
The tea's gone cold. Again.
…Fine, I'll warm it.
할 일은 늘 많아, 얘야.\n백 년 전 마녀들도 그렇게 말했지.\n…그러:
There's always a lot to do, child.
The witches said so a hundred years ago.
…Then they vanished one by one.
You're the one who should rest.
쯧, 말대꾸는.\n내가 수프 데울 테니 앉아.\n…할머니뻘 말은 듣는 거:
Tsk, talking back.
I'll warm the soup, you sit.
…You listen to your elders.
I laid a hand on the foundation stone.
It was warm. In winter.
Stone doesn't lie.
I won't write it on paper.
The stone will remember.
역시. 그 돌이 숨을 쉬는군.\n우리 유적의 돌도 그랬소.\n…그 유적은:
As I thought. That stone breathes.
The stone in our ruins did too.
…Those ruins are gone now.
…Understood.
Stone knows how to wait.
So do I.
…Cauldron.
Handle was loose.
Fixed it. Didn't ask.
고마워. 값은?: Thank you. What do I owe?
드워프 술집엔 노래가 있어요.\n'마녀의 솥엔 맥주가 끓는다'\n…진짜예:
Dwarven taverns have a song.
'In the witch's cauldron, ale is brewing'
…Is it true? Is there a recipe?
오늘은 제 노래만 불러요.\n올라가는 음으로요!:
Tonight only my songs.
Rising notes only!
감자…? 노래가 거짓말을!\n…아니다, 감자로도 술은 돼요.\n한 통 담:
Potato…? The song lied!
…No, wait, you can brew from potatoes.
Shall I start a barrel?
비약! 마시면 어떻게 돼요?\n…취하진 않아요? 그럼 됐어요.\n제 술이:
Elixirs! What happens when you drink one?
…Doesn't get you drunk? Then never mind.
My ale wins.
숲은 마녀사냥을 기억합니다.\n그때 요정들은 마녀를 숨겼지요.\n속이 빈:
The forest remembers the witch hunts.
The fae hid the witches then.
One in every hollow tree.
I will keep watch again tonight.
You sleep, my host.
인간의 책엔 없을 겁니다.\n요정은 책을 쓰지 않으니까요.\n나이테에 새:
It won't be in human books.
The fae do not write books.
We carve it into tree rings.
요정도 작은데 어떻게?: But the fae are so small.
…I have heard 'small'
a hundred times in the forest.
A hundred times, I was the one left standing.
맞혀 볼까요? 당신 모자,\n어젯밤 바람에 날아간 게 아니에요.\n…솔잎:
Want to guess? Your hat
didn't blow off in the wind last night.
…One of my pine-needle arrows is missing.
Tomorrow we play at targets.
Hats excluded.
The hat comes out of your lodging fee.
에에? 농담이었는데!\n…반은요. 반은 농담.\n내일 아침 지붕에서 찾아:
Whaat? It was a joke!
…Half. Half a joke.
I'll fetch it off the roof tomorrow.
당연하죠! 모자 끝의 술만 딱!\n…그런 걸 묻는 걸 보니\n당신도 요정:
Of course! Just the tassel on the tip!
…Asking that sort of thing,
you might have fae blood yourself.
마당의 가시 방책 말이오.\n뿌리가 아주 얕게 잠들어 있더군.\n…누가:
The thorn barricade in the yard.
Its roots sleep very shallow.
…Who planted it? Rough work.
Tomorrow I'll tend the lodge fence.
That one is still alive.
…그렇군. 거칠지만 살아 있소.\n정원사는 그 둘 중\n살아 있는 쪽을:
…I see. Rough, but alive.
Between the two,
a gardener chooses alive.
가시는 가지가 아니오.\n가시는 나무의 대답이지.\n묻는 게 많은 숲이면:
Thorns aren't branches.
Thorns are a tree's answer.
A forest asked many questions grows many thorns.
동쪽의 작은 분: The Little One in the East
저… 동쪽 숲에\n씨앗을 잘 받아 주는 분이 있어요.\n아주 작은… 마녀:
Um… in the eastern forest
there's someone who takes in seeds.
A very small… witch.
I'll give you a seed.
Keep it by the window… it will watch over you.
네… 모자가 자꾸 눈을 가려서\n손으로 올리는 분이요.\n…북쪽에도 한:
Yes… her hat keeps slipping over her eyes
and she pushes it up by hand.
…She said there's one in the north too.
씨앗을 왜 받아 줘?: Why would she take in seeds?
추워하는 씨앗을\n그냥 두지 못하는 분이라서요.\n…당신도 그렇죠? 창가:
She can't leave
a cold seed alone.
…You're the same, aren't you? The sill is warm.
숲의 전언입니다.\n북쪽 샘이 검게 변했습니다.\n당신 집 아래 돌을 노:
A message from the forest.
The northern spring has turned black.
The work of things after the stone beneath your house.
Do not let the fire go out.
The forest is watching. In a kindly way.
숲도 그렇게 보고 있습니다.\n그래서 저를 보냈습니다.\n경고가 아니라…:
So the forest sees.
That is why it sent me.
Not as a warning… as a greeting.
숲은 움직이지 않습니다.\n다만 기억합니다.\n…가끔 가지를 떨어뜨리지요:
The forest does not move.
It only remembers.
…And now and then drops a branch. On an enemy.
하아, 하아! 씨앗 배달인데요,\n수신인이 '굴뚝 연기 나는 집'이에요!:
Haah, haah! Seed delivery!
Addressed to 'the house with chimney smoke'!
…This is it, right? You have a chimney?
Back tomorrow! No I'm not!
…Haah, haah. Sleep first.
없어요! 이 숲엔 하나예요!\n다른 집은 다… 없어졌거든요.\n…그래서:
No! Just one in this forest!
The other houses are all… gone.
…That's why this one matters!
스물! …열아홉? 아, 하나는\n오다가 심었어요. 발이 미끄러져서요.\n:
Twenty! …Nineteen? Oh, one
got planted on the way. I slipped.
Next year there'll be a tree on the road!
어젯밤 꿈을 적었어요.\n네 사람이 등불을 나눠 들고\n갈림길에서 헤어지:
I wrote down last night's dream.
Four people sharing out lanterns
and parting at a crossroads.
…Yawn. Good night.
To the walls as well.
…하암. 알아요.\n이 집 벽이 꾸는 꿈이에요.\n벽이 오래되면 꿈을 꿔:
…Yawn. I know.
It's the dream these walls dream.
Old walls dream.
…The dream ends there.
But all four lanterns
were still lit. Yawn.
장터 애들이 그래요.\n마녀는 고블린을 솥에 넣는다고!\n…전 안 무서웠:
The market kids say
witches put goblins in the cauldron!
…I wasn't scared. From the third day on.
Next time I won't run.
…Not even strategically.
Only potatoes go in the cauldron.
감자! 좋아요! 감자는 친구예요!\n…그, 그럼 저는 뭘로 끓여요?\n아:
Potatoes! Great! Potatoes are friends!
…S-so what do I get cooked with?
No, not cooked, I mean, cooking!
If I were going to, I already would have.
히익! …농담이죠? 농담!\n하! 마녀님 농담 잘하시네!\n…문 쪽에 앉:
Eek! …Joking, right? Joking!
Ha! You're funny, Witch!
…Can I sit near the door?
양 일곱, 검은 양 하나.\n…어제는 검은 양이 없었소.\n내가 틀린 적:
Seven sheep, one black.
…Yesterday there was no black sheep.
I've never counted wrong.
Four windows, one door.
I'll recount tonight.
The black sheep was always there.
없었소. 셌지.\n…아니면 밤에 색이 바뀌었나?\n양이 그러오? 마녀 집:
It wasn't. I counted.
…Or did it change color in the night?
Do sheep do that? At a witch's house?
못 세는 건 못 참소.\n숫자가 안 맞으면 잠이 안 와.\n…오늘 밤은:
Can't stand not counting.
If the numbers are off, I can't sleep.
…Tonight I'll count traps instead of sheep.
그 지팡이, 참나무지?\n벼락 맞은 거!\n톱으로 썰면 얼마나 나올까…:
That staff, it's oak, right?
Lightning-struck!
Wonder how much I'd get sawing it up…
Tomorrow, only trees near the lodge.
Not looking at the staff. Really.
헤헤, 농담! 반쯤!\n…벼락 맞은 나무는 톱이 안 들어.\n아는데 괜히:
Hehe, joking! Half!
…A saw won't bite lightning-struck wood.
I know, but it's still exciting.
톱은 거짓말을 안 해!\n잘 들면 잘 든다, 안 들면 안 든다.\n고블린:
Saws don't lie!
Sharp is sharp, dull is dull.
Not like the goblin market.
그 등불이요, 기름이 없는데\n왜 타요? 만져 봤어요. 안 뜨거워요.\n:
That lantern, there's no oil,
so why does it burn? I touched it. Not hot.
…Oh, you said don't touch. Forgot.
새 주머니엔 좋은 것만요.\n이 집 단추 같은 거요. 안 가져가요!:
Only good things in the new pocket.
Like this house's buttons. Not taking them!
약속! 약속은 주머니에 안 들어가네…\n그럼 전 약속할게요.\n안 가져간:
Promises! Those don't fit in a pocket…
Then I promise.
I won't take it. Really. Probably.
Touch it again and the lodging doubles.
히익, 알았어요!\n…근데 두 배면 얼마예요?\n단추로도 돼요?:
Eek, okay!
…But how much is double?
Can I pay in buttons?
제안 하나! 숙박비 반값,\n대신 장터에서 선전해 드릴게요.\n'마녀의:
A proposal! Half-price lodging,
and I'll advertise you at the market.
'The Witch's Lodge. Does not eat guests.'
Full price for the room. No haggling.
…Just for today.
에이, 그럼 이렇게요.\n'마녀의 산장, 수프가 됨.'\n…그건 공짜로:
Aw, then how about this.
'The Witch's Lodge. Has soup.'
…That one's free. Because it's true.
그걸 빼면 손님이 안 와요!\n고블린은 그 말부터 봐요.\n…저도 그거:
Drop that and nobody comes!
Goblins read that line first.
…It's what brought me here.
이 몸 그릭, 워록을 봤어요!\n숲 안쪽 동굴에서! 수염이 바닥까지!\n:
I, Grik, saw a warlock!
In a cave deep in the forest! Beard to the floor!
…From behind, though. Probably a warlock.
This house goes on the map.
Big. The biggest.
곰! …곰도 워록일 수 있죠!\n워록은 사라졌다잖아요.\n곰으로 변했을지:
A bear! …A bear could be a warlock!
They say the warlocks vanished.
Who's to say they didn't turn into bears!
'거기 서'라고… 아니, '꺼져'였나.\n…말은 안 했어요. 사실.\n근:
'Halt'… no, maybe 'get lost.'
…He didn't say anything. Honestly.
But his eyes said it! Definitely!
모르는 얼굴의 동전: The Coin With a Stranger's Face
숲에서 주운 동전이요.\n얼굴이 고블린도 인간도 아니에요.\n…마녀사냥:
A coin I found in the forest.
The face isn't goblin or human.
…Could it be from before the witch hunts?
Sell the lantern to me, and no one else.
I'll pay generously.
워록…! 그럼 값은\n'못 매김'이에요. 최고 등급이죠.\n…볼 때마다:
A warlock…! Then its value
is 'beyond appraisal.' The top grade.
…The way it smiles a little more each time is a bonus.
팔 생각 없어요.\n값 못 매기는 건 안 파는 게 원칙.\n…이 집 등불:
No intention to.
I never sell what I can't price.
…That's why I can't buy your lantern either.
…늑대 무리는 마녀를 기억한다.\n마녀사냥 때 산을 넘게 해 준 것.\n:
…The wolf packs remember the witches.
They got us over the mountains in the hunts.
A debt belongs to the pack. To me too.
…That's what humans say.
Wolves are different.
Tonight I lie down by the door.
…The pack left me.
In this house
we don't speak of that.
I see better at night.
You didn't sleep last night.
You checked the window three times.
You can put out the light.
I can see.
Yes.
You skipped the fourth.
Because I'd looked.
Lynx sleep by day.
…The sheep are loud here by day.
It's fine. I fold my ears.
으음… 곰 수인한텐 전설이 있어.\n'마녀의 집에서 겨울잠을 자면\n봄에:
Hmm… bear-kin have a legend.
'Hibernate in a witch's house
and you wake twice over in spring.'
I'll leave half a jar of honey.
…Just half. Winter is long.
…몰라. 전설은 거기까지야.\n몸집일 수도, 꿀일 수도.\n…몸집은 곤란:
…Don't know. The legend stops there.
Could be size, could be honey.
…Size would be trouble. Small door.
Sleep here and that's a hundred nights' rent.
Hmm… a hundred nights.
In honey, that's… three jars.
…Could I pay half a jar at a time?
저, 저기요! 마녀님은\n토끼를 안 드시죠? 드시죠? 안 드시죠?\n…동:
U-um, excuse me! Witch, you don't
eat rabbits, right? You do? You don't?
…The one in the east said she doesn't.
I like the corner of the room.
Somewhere like a burrow… is safe.
히익! …아, 손님이 내는 요금이요?\n제가 먹히는 게 아니고요?\n…휴:
Eek! …Oh, a charge the guest pays?
Not me getting eaten?
…Phew. Then I'll gather more herbs.
동쪽 분을 알아?: You know the one in the east?
네! 모자가 큰 분이요.\n저만큼 겁이 많으신데\n다친 건 절대 안 두고:
Yes! The one with the big hat.
She's as timid as I am,
but she never leaves a wounded thing alone.
길잡이 값은 안 받을게요.\n대신 하나만. 이 숲 길이\n마녀사냥 뒤로:
No charge for guiding today.
Just one thing. Is it true the forest roads
changed after the witch hunts?
No shortcuts for a while.
Even if it takes half a day longer.
역시! 그래서 꼬리가 헷갈렸구나.\n숲이 손님을 고르는 거네요.\n…저는:
I knew it! That's why my tail got confused.
So the forest picks its guests.
…I passed, right? I'm in?
아는 척은 직업상 하죠.\n모르는 걸 아는 게 진짜 길잡이고요.\n…멋있:
Pretending to know is part of the job.
Knowing what you don't know makes a real guide.
…That sounded good, didn't it?
…Load.
One is yours.
…Didn't see who handed it over.
응.\n'북쪽 등불 집'이라고 했어.\n…열어 보면 알겠지. 난 안 열어:
Yes.
They said 'the lantern house in the north.'
…You'll know when you open it. I don't open.
…Already paid.
Half a jar of honey.
…The bear gave it.
하늘에서 보면 알아요.\n이 세상 네 귀퉁이에\n밤마다 등불 하나씩 켜져:
From the sky you can tell.
At the four corners of this world
a lantern lights up every night.
I'll sleep when the sun is up.
Thank you for the light in the window.
Yes. Tonight too.
…One flickered a little,
but owls are never wrong.
I won't. Owls fly
toward what they see.
Never toward whom they tell.
오크는 마녀사냥에 안 갔다.\n인간이 횃불을 나눠 줬지만\n우리 법에 ':
Orcs did not join the witch hunts.
Humans handed out torches,
but our law has no 'burn the guest.'
Sleep, innkeeper.
The one who owes stays awake.
…좋다 싫다는 작은 말이다.\n오크는 법을 말한다.\n지붕을 빌린 빚은:
…Like and dislike are small words.
Orcs speak of law.
A borrowed roof is repaid with the sword.
Good. I stand at the door.
A door I stand before
has never opened.
이 집 사냥꾼이 누구야?\n토끼 셋에 하루? 하!\n난 아침 먹기 전에:
Who's the hunter around here?
Three rabbits in a day? Ha!
I get five before breakfast.
Dinner's on me tonight.
Three rabbits. Get the pot.
당연하지! 솥 꺼내!\n…토끼가 안 보이는데.\n숲이 날 피하나? 명성이:
Of course! Get the pot!
…I don't see any rabbits.
Is the forest avoiding me? My reputation?
That hunter shoots at night too.
흥, 나도 밤에… 자지.\n오크는 밤에 먹고 자는 거야.\n…알았어, 내:
Hmph, at night I… sleep.
Orcs eat and sleep at night.
…Fine, tomorrow I'll stay up.
Haha! I apologized to the door earlier.
'I'm sorry, thank you.'
…The door's wood too. It didn't answer.
내일은 말 없는 나무만 벨게.\n하하! 문 조심할게!:
Tomorrow only the silent trees.
Haha! I'll mind the door!
나무도 대답은 안 해!\n근데 말하면 도끼가 가벼워져.\n…말 안 하면:
Trees don't either!
But saying it makes the axe lighter.
…Not saying it makes it heavy. Strange, eh?
뭐라고 대답하길 바랐어?: What did you want it to say?
'괜찮다.' 그 한마디.\n…주인이 대신 해 줘도 돼.\n하하! 농담!:
'It's alright.' Just that.
…You could say it for the door.
Haha! Joking! …Half.
스승이 말했어요.\n'재가 깨끗한 집을 찾으면\n마녀가 사는 집이다. 믿:
My teacher told me.
'Find a house where the ash is clean
and a witch lives there. You can trust it.'
I'll sleep by the hearth tonight.
So the ash stays warm.
재로 그걸 알아?: You can tell that from ash?
재는 뭘 태웠는지 말해요.\n이 집 재는 장작만 태웠어요.\n…다른 건:
Ash tells you what was burned.
This house's ash is only firewood.
…Nothing else at all.
…Deep in the forest.
She went to save the roots.
She hasn't come back. Yet.
뼈를 던졌다.\n네 개가 네 방향으로 떨어지더군.\n…네 자매 얘긴 안:
I cast the bones.
Four fell in four directions.
…No need to tell me about four sisters. The bones did.
Sleep. I'll watch the bones.
Until the fourth.
'Not yet.'
The bones rarely say that.
Usually they say 'already.'
That's not an omen, that's a rumor.
하! 소문은 사람이 던지고\n점은 뼈가 던지지.\n둘 다 가끔 맞는다,:
Ha! People cast rumors,
bones cast omens.
Both are right now and then, child.
북쪽 등불 집: The Lantern House in the North
조상의 길이 이 집을 지나오.\n백 년 전 기록에도\n'북쪽 등불 집에서:
The ancestors' road passes this house.
Even a record from a hundred years back says
'we rested at the lantern house in the north.'
I'll sleep by the fire.
They say the ancestors did too.
There was a witch here then too.
그렇겠지. 마녀가 없으면\n등불이 없고, 등불이 없으면\n길이 없소. 오:
So there was. Without a witch,
no lantern; without a lantern,
no road. Orcs know that.
You asked if it was the same fire.
…대답은 들었소.\n오늘 밤 그 불 옆에서 자면\n조상과 같은 꿈을 꾸겠:
…I have my answer.
Sleep beside that fire tonight
and I'll dream what the ancestors dreamed.
부엌 봤어요! 감자, 소금, 버섯.\n…이게 다예요? 진짜로요?\n오크:
I saw the kitchen! Potato, salt, mushroom.
…That's all? Really?
An orc cook could weep.
Cooking again! Double!
Everyone eats. Inside.
그 말 벽에도 써 있더라고요!\n좋아요, 추가 요금 낼게요.\n대신 솥은:
It's written on the wall too!
Fine, I'll pay the extra.
But I take the pot. Tonight!
손님들이 착한 거예요!\n아니면 배가 고프거나.\n…둘 다인가. 어쨌든:
The guests are just kind!
Or hungry.
…Both, maybe. Anyway, I'm doubling the batch!
